assignments.title: 14.7 Primary Source Report: Keynes and the Peace of 1919
assignments.html:
PRIMARY SOURCE REPORT
Keynes and the Peace of 1919
A book that helped shape how people judged the treaty.
Report · 16 points · Word document upload
♦ ─ ♦ ─ ♦
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then write your report in Word and submit it as the submission box below describes.
THE TASK

Write a report of 450 to 650 words in Word. Answer all four questions below, in order, each under its own heading. Use the Keynes excerpt and “The Wreckage: Four Empires Gone and the Senate's No”. Put short quotations in quotation marks and cite each one in a footnote.

You will be graded on the quality of your argument, not on which side you take.

YOUR REPORT

1. Keynes was inside the conference and then resigned. What does he say the peacemakers cared about, and what does he say they ignored? Use two short quotations. Then say what his position lets him see, and what might bias him.

2. Keynes writes, “The clock cannot be set back.” Explain in your own words what he thinks will happen to Europe if the victors try to set it back. Connect your answer to the reparations described in “The Wreckage: Four Empires Gone and the Senate's No”.

3. “The Wreckage: Four Empires Gone and the Senate's No” says Keynes’s book may have made the treaty harder to enforce. Explain how a book could have that effect. Why might later historians say that Keynes exaggerated?

4. Suppose Wilson had accepted Lodge’s reservations in November 1919 and the Senate had approved the treaty. How might the argument over whether the treaty was too harsh or too weakly enforced have changed? Say what you think would have been different, and what you cannot know.

GRADING RUBRIC (16 pts)

SUBMISSION

Write your report in Word and save it to your OneDrive folder. Then open this assignment in Canvas, choose the OneDrive tab, select your file, and submit.

Your teacher will read your report and score it with the rubric above.

MODULE INTRODUCTION
Module Introduction: The Peace That Failed
Survey · 3 questions · not graded
♦ ─ ♦ ─ ♦
Before you start

Welcome to The Peace That Failed. Answer the questions below before you open the first lesson. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting. This survey is not graded.

This module's goals:
  • Explain who made the Treaty of Versailles and what each leader wanted.
  • Describe what replaced the four fallen empires and why the new states were fragile.
  • Trace why the United States did not join the League of Nations.

discussions.title: 14.8 Discussion: Was Versailles too harsh, or too weakly enforced?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Was Versailles too harsh, or too weakly enforced?
A peace too heavy to forgive, or too weak to enforce?
Graded discussion · 10 points · one post and one reply
♦ ─ ♦ ─ ♦
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then post your answer to the prompt below, and reply to one classmate.
DISCUSSION PROMPT

This week’s question: Was Versailles too harsh, or too weakly enforced?

Choose a side, or argue for a third view. Name at least two specific decisions from 1918 to 1920 that shaped the outcome, and explain how each might have gone another way.

Write 150 to 250 words. State one claim you believe is true. Then explain why, using the specific evidence named above. Keep to what the lessons and the sources show. If you are guessing, say so.

Then add one sentence on responsibility. Who bore it for what followed: the men who wrote the treaty, the nations that did not enforce it, or the United States for staying out? Name whom you hold responsible and why.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a fact or decision they did not use. If not, say politely where you think it falls short, and give your reason.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
CriteriaSubstantive (full credit)Thin (partial credit)Missing (no credit)
